reason: I cook maybe one weekend day and order delivery the rest of the week, and I already ask a free AI chat for recipes when I need one. I might open the five free dishes once, but I'm not pre-paying for twelve more before I know I'd even use the free ones.
objection: A free AI chat already tells me how to make tom yum or pad see ew, so I don't see what the paid pack gives me that I can't get for nothing. And paying in advance for something not delivered yet, from an app I've never heard of, feels backwards.
would_change_my_mind: If I actually cooked the free dishes on a couple of weekends and the step-by-step and the 'it didn't work' help came out clearly better than my free chat, I'd pay for the pack once it exists, not as a pre-order.
